_comment: Given names and surnames for eight Indian languages that had none at all.
There is no register to read. India's Census runs to some two hundred tables under GODL
and not one counts names; Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Nepal and Bangladesh publish nothing
comparable. Wikidata carries thousands of names for European languages and fewer than
five each for Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam and Gujarati. Five hundred million
people, and this corpus answered for all of them in English.
naamapadam is a named-entity dataset -- 5.78M sentences of Indian-language text with
person spans marked -- released CC0 by AI4Bharat. CC0 is the only reason it is usable:
every other Indian name dataset found alongside it was built from a leaked Facebook
dump, from 'public records', from unnamed sources, or scraped from Wiktionary.
SINGLE TOKENS, NEVER A PAIR. The spans are read for their parts and the parts counted
separately; a given name and the surname beside it are never stored together. What ships
is a vocabulary of name-words with frequencies -- a register in shape, if not in origin.
It is not the list of people the sentences were about, and this project has already
refused three such lists.
It ships knowingly imperfect. The tags were projected automatically from English word
alignments rather than read by anyone, so roughly a third of what survives filtering
carries a case ending: Tamil's `panchaaliyin` is `Bhansali's`, not `Bhansali`. Stripping
those needs a morphological analyser per language, which is eleven sets of rules nobody
here can verify -- the same reason decoy-authored is English only. The trade is a locale
mostly right in its own language against no locale at all, and for fixture data that is
the better half. See IndicNamesAdapter for the four filters and what each removes.
name: Naamapadam (AI4Bharat) v1.0
